rule: A metro gets an Encampment when (a) an active non-Guard MIRTA installation of tier 'major' or 'base' (not a small reserve centre or office) lies in one of its member counties, or one of the restricted ranges covers one of its hexes, and (b) residents in the armed forces (ACS 5-year B23025_006, by place of residence, summed over the member counties) are at least 1% of the population 16 and over, or at least 2,000 and at least 0.3%. Tier: 'fortress' at 3% or more, otherwise 'garrison'. 'naval' when the metro's qualifying Navy and Marine Corps installations outweigh its Army and Air Force ones, counting a 'major' installation as 4 and a 'base' as 1.

rules.tier: No per-installation headcount is published, so size comes from the MIRTA boundary and component: 'major' = an active-duty site (Army, Navy, Air Force incl. Space Force, Marine Corps, or other DoD) with a boundary of at least 100 km² (about 25,000 acres), or one of 28 flagship active-duty bases on small land picked by this project (fleet bases, air logistics complexes, headquarters posts such as Naval Station Norfolk; flagged curated); 'base' = any other active-duty site of at least 1 km², or a Guard or Reserve site of at least 10 km² (Guard and Reserve are never 'major'); 'site' = everything else. Parcels under 1 km² that share a hex and component with a larger installation are folded into the nearest one and listed as its parts; the Barry M. Goldwater Range's Air Force and Marine Corps halves are one installation.
rules.ranges: The 30 largest MIRTA boundaries in the lower 48 (by area, at least 400 km²; sites with several boundaries are summed), active or semi-active. Their cells are the hexes whose centre lies inside the boundary; a range that covers no hex centre is shown on the one hex holding its point. A hex is about 1,600 km², so small ranges are drawn larger than they are. A range's state is its installation's state (where the installation point lies), so a range that spills over a state line (Fort Bliss: TX headquarters, mostly New Mexico ground) is listed under the same state as its installation; the state holding most of its hexes is given too.
rules.encampment: A metro gets an Encampment when (a) an active non-Guard MIRTA installation of tier 'major' or 'base' (not a small reserve centre or office) lies in one of its member counties, or one of the restricted ranges covers one of its hexes, and (b) residents in the armed forces (ACS 5-year B23025_006, by place of residence, summed over the member counties) are at least 1% of the population 16 and over, or at least 2,000 and at least 0.3%. Tier: 'fortress' at 3% or more, otherwise 'garrison'. 'naval' when the metro's qualifying Navy and Marine Corps installations outweigh its Army and Air Force ones, counting a 'major' installation as 4 and a 'base' as 1.
rules.installations: MIRTA installation points in the lower 48 that are active, semi-active or in caretaker status (closed and excess sites are left out). A point just offshore is placed on the nearest US land hex. Large boundaries (200 km² or more) also list the hexes whose centre they cover. Each site is placed in the state where its point lies, which can differ from the state MIRTA files it under.
rules.names: Names follow MIRTA FY2025 except seven Army posts whose names the Army restored on 10 June 2025 (Fort Cavazos is now Fort Hood, Fort Johnson is now Fort Polk, Fort Novosel is now Fort Rucker, Fort Eisenhower is now Fort Gordon, Fort Gregg-Adams is now Fort Lee, Fort Walker is now Fort A.P. Hill, Fort Barfoot is now Fort Pickett; source: https://www.army.mil/article/286223/army_to_change_names_of_seven_installations). The MIRTA spelling is kept alongside the current name.

caveats: Installation points and boundaries: DoD MIRTA (not every DoD site is listed; Coast Guard sites are not DoD). No per-base personnel figure is published, so bases are sized by area, not troops, plus a short curated list of flagship bases on small land. Personnel are by duty state (DMDC), excluding classified data and most deployed or temporary-duty personnel. Contract dollars follow the place of performance (OLDCC), not where bases are. Armed forces by county count where service members live (ACS). Seven Army posts carry the names the Army restored in June 2025 (Fort Hood, Fort Polk, Fort Rucker, Fort Gordon, Fort Lee, Fort A.P. Hill, Fort Pickett); MIRTA FY2025 still uses their 2023 names, which the data keeps alongside.
